item.text:
I used two direct search passes and stopped there. The record for 5B.4 is mostly reform-oriented, but still incomplete and state-heavy.

1. **[Pakistan: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on Economic Policies with Pakistan for 37-month Extended Fund Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff)** — Publisher: IMF; Date: 2024-07-12; URL: https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff; Claim: The IMF says the program included broadening the tax base, improving SOE management, strengthening competition, securing a level playing field for investment, and scaling up human capital and social protection. This is strong positive evidence that Sharif’s government was trying to make market rules more predictable and less rent-distorting. QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.1, 5B.3.

2. **[IMF Executive Board Concludes 2024 Article IV Consultation for Pakistan and Approves 37-month Extended Arrangement](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr)** — Publisher: IMF; Date: 2024-09-27; URL: https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr; Claim: The IMF says the new program aimed to entrench macro stability, strengthen competition, remove state distortions, improve the FDI regime, reform SOEs, and support a fairer business environment. It also says investment remained very low, the tax base too narrow, and the state too large in the economy, so the fair-rules agenda was real but unfinished. QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.3, 5B.1.

3. **[Pakistan: Second and Final Review Under the Stand-By Arrangement](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/05/10/pakistan-second-and-final-review-under-the-stand-by-arrangement-press-release-staff-report-548741)** — Publisher: IMF; Date: 2024-05-10; URL: https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/05/10/pakistan-second-and-final-review-under-the-stand-by-arrangement-press-release-staff-report-548741; Claim: The IMF says sustainable recovery required strict fiscal targets, a market-determined exchange rate, better tax collection, SOE reform, and governance/anti-corruption measures, with more inclusive growth and job creation still dependent on continued structural reform. This supports a rule-setting intent aligned with entrepreneurship and job creation, but also shows the framework was still under construction. QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.3, 5B.1.

4. **[PAKISTAN: Reform Implementation Remains Critical for Continued Economic Recovery and Poverty Reduction, says World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank)** — Publisher: World Bank; Date: 2024-10-10; URL: https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank; Claim: The World Bank says Pakistan still needed reforms to the tax system, inefficient spending, untargeted subsidies, the large state presence, and barriers to trade and investment. That is negative evidence that fair rules were not yet fully in place even after recovery began. QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.3.

5. **[Pakistan PM unveils broader plan to sell most state-owned firms](https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-unveils-broader-plan-to-sell-most-state-owned-firms/2084587/)** — Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint; Date: 2024-05-14; URL: https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-unveils-broader-plan-to-sell-most-state-owned-firms/2084587/; Claim: Sharif said all state-owned enterprises would be privatized except strategic ones, framing it as saving taxpayers’ money and repairing weak public finances. This is concrete pro-competition, pro-investment evidence, though still only an announced reform rather than a completed structural change. QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.1, 5B.3.

6. **[Pakistan’s government ends power deals early to cut costs](https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298)** — Publisher: Reuters via Dawn; Date: 2024-10-10; URL: https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298; Claim: The government renegotiated power-purchase contracts to cut electricity tariffs and save about Rs60 billion a year. That helps entrepreneurship and job creation by lowering input costs, but it also shows ongoing state management of prices rather than a clean market liberalization. QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.3.

7. **[Pakistan 2024 Article IV Consultation and Request for an Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152)** — Publisher: IMF; Date: 2024-10-10; URL: https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152; Claim: The IMF says Pakistan still had a narrow tax base, weak governance, an outsized state role, and a business environment that hindered investment. This is the clearest negative evidence against a fully fair, entrepreneurship-friendly rule system in 2024. QIDs: 5B.4, 5B.3.

Search gap: I did not find strong 2024 evidence on direct property-rights enforcement, land/title reform, contract-enforcement reform, or entrepreneurship-specific legal changes beyond the IMF/World Bank program language and SOE/tariff actions. The evidence base is much stronger on macro reform and state-distortion reduction than on actual property-rights outcomes.
